arxiv-2102-11505.title: Effects of ground-state correlations on damping of giant dipole resonances in L ​ S LS closed shell nuclei
arxiv-2102-11505.creator: Mitsuru Tohyama
arxiv-2102-11505.description: Abstract The effects of ground-state correlations on the damping of isovector giant dipole resonances in L ​ S LS closed shell nuclei 16 O and 40 Ca are studied using extended random-phase-approximation (RPA) approaches derived from the time-dependent density-matrix theory.

arxiv-2202-07444.title: A Multipurpose Reduced Mechanism for Ethanol Combustion Journal: Combustion and flame
arxiv-2202-07444.creator: Alejandro Millán-Merino, Eduardo Fernández-Tarrazo, Mario Sánchez-Sanz, Forman A. Williams
arxiv-2202-07444.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alejandro Millán-Merino, Eduardo Fernández-Tarrazo, Mario Sánchez-Sanz, Forman A. Williams. New multipurpose skeletal and reduced chemical-kinetic mechanisms for ethanol combustion are developed, along the same philosophical lines followed in our previous work on methanol. arxiv-2203-12164.title: Application of Co-Kriging and Ordinary Kriging for Selecting Additional Well Locations
arxiv-2203-12164.creator: Rong Lu, Colorado School of Mines
arxiv-2203-12164.description: Abstract Well performance index (WPI), which is an indicator on how much producing potential a well has, is proposed for Cana Field using the available information from the completion database. I used ordinary kriging and co-kriging to create interpolation maps for WPI across the region.

arxiv-2205-00248.title: Regularity theory for a new class of fractional parabolic stochastic evolution equations
arxiv-2205-00248.creator: Kristin Kirchner and Joshua Willems
arxiv-2205-00248.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kristin Kirchner and Joshua Willems. A new class of fractional-order stochastic evolution equations of the form ( ∂ t + A ) γ X ( t ) = W ˙ Q ( t ) (\partial_{t}+A)^{\gamma}X(t)=\dot{W}^{Q}(t) , t ∈ [ 0 , T ] t\in[0,T] , γ ∈ ( 0 , ∞ ) \gamma\in(0,\infty) , is introduced, where − A -A generates a C 0 C_{0} -semigroup on a separable Hilbert space H H and the spatiotemporal driving noise W ˙ Q \dot{W}^{Q} is the

arxiv-2205-09931.title: Fork Entropy: Assessing the Diversity of Open Source Software Projects’ Forks
arxiv-2205-09931.creator: Liang Wang, Baihui Sang, Zhiwen Zheng, Jierui Zhang, Xiangchen Wu, Xianping Tao
arxiv-2205-09931.description: Abstract On open source software (OSS) platforms such as GitHub, forking and accepting pull-requests is an important approach for OSS projects to receive contributions, especially from external contributors who cannot directly commit into the source repositories. Having a large number of forks is often considered as an indicator of a project being popular.

arxiv-2211-03750.title: Effect of roughness on the transport of an overdamped Brownian particle
arxiv-2211-03750.creator: Prathyusha S Nair
arxiv-2211-03750.description: Abstract We study the transport of an overdamped Brownian particle in a tilted rough potential driven by a gaussian white noise.We conisder various forms of rough potentials to analyse the effect of roughness on the diffusion and current generated.The variation of current, diffusion coefficient, and peclet number with the static tilting force, amplitude of roughness and temperature were studied.

arxiv-2303-07853.title: ReFit: A Framework for Refinement of Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation using Object Border Fitting for Medical Images
arxiv-2303-07853.creator: Bharath Srinivas Prabakaran, Erik Ostrowski ⋆, Muhammad Shafique
arxiv-2303-07853.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bharath Srinivas Prabakaran, Erik Ostrowski ⋆, Muhammad Shafique. Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) relying only on image-level supervision is a promising approach to deal with the need for Segmentation networks, especially for generating a large number of pixel-wise masks in a given dataset. However, most state-of-the-art image-level WSSS techniques lack an understanding of the geometric features embedded in the images since the network cannot derive any object boundary information from just image-level labels.

arxiv-2304-00363.title: Automatic Authorship Attribution in the work of Tirso de Molina
arxiv-2304-00363.creator: Miguel Cavadas Docampo, Pablo Gamallo
arxiv-2304-00363.description: Abstract Automatic Authorship Attribution (AAA) is the result of applying tools and techniques from Digital Humanities to authorship attribution studies. Through a quantitative and statistical approach this discipline can draw further conclusions about renowned authorship issues which traditional critics have been dealing with for centuries, opening a new door to style comparison.

arxiv-2304-05049.title: Static Entanglement Analysis of Quantum Programs
arxiv-2304-05049.creator: Shangzhou Xia, Jianjun Zhao
arxiv-2304-05049.description: Abstract Quantum entanglement plays a crucial role in quantum computing. Entangling information has important implications for understanding the behavior of quantum programs and avoiding entanglement-induced errors. Entanglement analysis is a static code analysis technique that determines which qubit may entangle with another qubit and establishes an entanglement graph to represent the whole picture of interactions between entangled qubits.

arxiv-2308-01184.title: Partial Label Supervision for Agnostic Generative Noisy Label Learning
arxiv-2308-01184.creator: Fengbei Liu, Chong Wang, Yuanhong Chen, Yuyuan Liu, Gustavo Carneiro
arxiv-2308-01184.description: Abstract Noisy label learning has been tackled with both discriminative and generative approaches. Despite the simplicity and efficiency of discriminative methods, generative models offer a more principled way of disentangling clean and noisy labels and estimating the label transition matrix.

arxiv-2308-09513.title: Anisotropic Virtual Gain and Large Tuning of Particles’ Scattering by Complex-Frequency Excitations Preprint: Submitted to PRL
arxiv-2308-09513.creator: Grigorios P. Zouros, Iridanos Loulas, Evangelos Almpanis, Alex Krasnok, Kosmas L. Tsakmakidis
arxiv-2308-09513.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Grigorios P. Zouros, Iridanos Loulas, Evangelos Almpanis, Alex Krasnok, Kosmas L. Tsakmakidis. Active tuning of the scattering of particles and metasurfaces is a highly sought-after property for a host of electromagnetic and photonic applications, but it normally requires challenging-to-control tunable (reconfigurable) or active (gain) media. Here, we introduce the concepts of anisotropic virtual gain and oblique Kerker effect, where a completely lossy anisotropic medium behaves exactly as its anisotropic gain counterpart upon excitation by a synthetic complex-frequency wave.

arxiv-2310-15506.title: Topology Optimization with Text-Guided Stylization
arxiv-2310-15506.creator: Shengze Zhong, Parinya Punpongsanon, Daisuke Iwai, Kosuke Sato
arxiv-2310-15506.description: Abstract We propose an approach for the generation of topology-optimized structures with text-guided appearance stylization. This methodology aims to enrich the concurrent design of a structure’s physical functionality and aesthetic appearance. Users can effortlessly input descriptive text to govern the style of the structure.

arxiv-2402-01505.title: Code-Switched Language Identification is Harder Than You Think
arxiv-2402-01505.creator: Laurie Burchell, Alexandra Birch, Robert P. Thompson, Kenneth Heafield
arxiv-2402-01505.description: Abstract cs ( cs ) is a very common phenomenon in written and spoken communication but one that is handled poorly by many nlp ( nlp ) applications. Looking to the application of building cs corpora, we explore cs lid ( lid ) for corpus building.

arxiv-2410-12492.title: End-to-end Planner Training for Language Modeling
arxiv-2410-12492.creator: Nathan Cornille, Florian Mai, Jingyuan Sun, Marie-Francine Moens
arxiv-2410-12492.description: Abstract Through end-to-end training to predict the next token, LLMs have become valuable tools for various tasks. Enhancing their core training in language modeling can improve numerous downstream applications. A successful approach to enhance language modeling uses a separate planning module to predict abstract labels of future sentences and conditions the LM on these predictions.

arxiv-2501-07398.title: An ontology-based description of nano computed tomography measurements in electronic laboratory notebooks: from metadata schema to first user experience
arxiv-2501-07398.creator: F. Kirchner, D.C.F. Wieland, S. Irvine, S. Schimek, J. Reimers, R. Aversa, A. Boubnov, C. Lucas, S. Flenner, I. Greving, A. Lopes Marinho, T.M. Wong, R. Willumeit-Römer, C. Eschke, B. Zeller-Plumhoff
arxiv-2501-07398.description: Abstract Abstract In recent years, the importance of well-documented metadata has been discussed increasingly in many research fields. Making all metadata generated during scientific research available in a findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) manner remains a significant challenge for researchers across fields.

arxiv-2502-14267.title: Money Recognition for the Visually Impaired: A Case Study on Sri Lankan Banknotes
arxiv-2502-14267.creator: Akshaan Bandara
arxiv-2502-14267.description: Abstract Currency note recognition is a critical accessibility need for blind individuals, as identifying banknotes accurately can impact their independence and security in financial transactions. Several traditional and technological initiatives have been taken to date. Nevertheless, these approaches are less user-friendly and have made it more challenging for blind people to identify banknotes.

arxiv-2505-18732.title: Mobile Manipulation Planning for Tabletop Rearrangement
arxiv-2505-18732.creator: Jiaming Hu, Jiawei Wang, Henrik I Christensen
arxiv-2505-18732.description: Abstract Efficient tabletop rearrangement planning seeks to find high-quality solutions while minimizing total cost. However, the task is challenging due to object dependencies and limited buffer space for temporary placements. The complexity increases for mobile robots, which must navigate around the table with restricted access.

arxiv-2508-09102.title: Covariance as a commutator
arxiv-2508-09102.creator: Carlos García Meixide
arxiv-2508-09102.description: Abstract The covariance between real finite variance random variables can be expressed as the commutator of taking expectations and multiplying, both viewed as operators extended to act jointly on pairs of functions. The efficient influence curve of the mean represents a centering operator which we demonstrate to interact with expectations and products through simple commutator identities.

arxiv-2606-29938.title: LatentRevise: Learning from Zero-Hit Reasoning
arxiv-2606-29938.creator: Yiqiu Guo Xueting Han Qi Jia Guangtao Zhai Jing Bai, [0.4em] Fudan University Microsoft Research Asia, [0.2em] Shanghai AI Laboratory Shanghai Jiao Tong University [0.2em]

pmc-10499836.title: Enhanced antibody-antigen structure prediction from molecular docking using AlphaFold2
pmc-10499836.creator: Francis Gaudreault, Christopher R. Corbeil, Traian Sulea
pmc-10499836.description: Predicting the structure of antibody-antigen complexes has tremendous value in biomedical research but unfortunately suffers from a poor performance in real-life applications. AlphaFold2 (AF2) has provided renewed hope for improvements in the field of protein–protein docking but has shown limited success against antibody-antigen complexes due to the lack of co-evolutionary constraints.

pmc-10716652.title: Still air resistance during walking and running
pmc-10716652.creator: Matteo M. Pecchiari, Mario A. Legramandi, Giuseppe Gibertini, Giovanni A. Cavagna
pmc-10716652.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In everyday life during terrestrial locomotion our body interacts with two media opposing the forward movement of the body: the ground and the air. Whereas the work done to overcome the ground reaction force has been extensively studied, the work done to overcome still air resistance has been only indirectly estimated by means of theoretical studies and by measurements of the force exerted on puppets simulating the geometry of the human body.

pmc-11528975.title: Providing Emotional Support During the Process of Multiple Sclerosis Diagnosis (PrEliMS): A Feasibility Randomised Controlled Trial
pmc-11528975.creator: Roshan das Nair, Jacqueline R Mhizha-Murira, Gogem Topcu, Tierney Tindall, Clare Bale, Nima Moghaddam, Grit Scheffler-Ansari, Avril Drummond, Deborah Fitzsimmons, Nikos Evangelou
pmc-11528975.description: ObjectivesTo evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an emotional support programme for newly diagnosed people with multiple sclerosis.DesignThree-arm, mixed methods, randomised controlled trial comparing usual care, versus usual care plus nurse-specialist support, versus usual care plus nurse-specialist support plus peer support.ParticipantsCommunity-dwelling adults within two years of diagnosis or undergoing diagnosis.

pmc-12670424.title: Expanding the Scope of PROTACs: Opportunities and Challenges in Topical Delivery
pmc-12670424.creator: Laura Gioiello, Rita Maria Concetta Di Martino, Tracey Pirali
pmc-12670424.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as a novel therapeutic modality primarily through systemic administration. Recently, their topical use has drawn increasing attention, offering a promising strategy to achieve localized protein degradation while minimizing systemic toxicity. This miniperspective highlights key advances in the development of topical PROTACs, exemplified by AH-001 and GT20029, androgen receptor degraders, both in clinical trials for androgenetic alopecia, with GT20029 also evaluated for acne.

pmc-12742053.title: Improving access to inpatient palliative care for patients with end-stage liver disease: a quality improvement project
pmc-12742053.creator: Elvina Ward, Georgina Hanbury, Lucia Possamai, Thomas Rassam
pmc-12742053.description: BackgroundEnd-stage liver disease (ESLD) is a terminal diagnosis with a poor prognosis and an accelerating mortality rate in the UK. Limited research suggests that patients with ESLD have unmet palliative care (PC) needs, likely due to various factors, including difficulty predicting prognosis and lack of clear specialist palliative care (SPC) referral criteria.

pmc-13067760.title: Structural MRI assessment of hypothalamic alterations and cognitive implications in adolescents with rapid pubertal progression
pmc-13067760.creator: Lulu Lin, Pingyi Zhu, Donghui Zhou, Shundan Zhao, Peilong Pan, Xiaozheng Liu, Zhihan Yan, Min Dai
pmc-13067760.description: BackgroundRapid pubertal progression involves hormonal and hypothalamic adaptations, yet its neurocognitive implications remain unclear. Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), a key mediator of growth and neurodevelopment, is closely linked to pubertal processes. This study aims to investigate IGF-1-associated hypothalamic structural changes and their cognitive consequences in adolescents with rapid pubertal progression (Tanner stage advancement ≥ 1 within 3–6 months).

pmc-13401034.title: Divergent effects of roasting on the volatile profiles and metabolomes of Pinus pumila and Pinus koraiensis nuts
pmc-13401034.creator: Yong Yu, Qingzhu Nie, Xiaolong Chen, Yu Di, Aiyuan Wang, Hongwei Yang, Kaiming Ren
pmc-13401034.description: To evaluate the effects of roasting and varietal differences on pine nut flavour, an electronic nose, HS-SPME-GC-Orbitrap MS, and non-targeted metabolomics were used to compare the volatile profiles and metabolomes of raw and roasted Pinus pumila (PP) and Pinus koraiensis (PK) nuts. Roasting markedly amplified the metabolic and flavour differences between the two species.

pmc-13661827.title: Light as a master switch: a critical review of photonanozymes from design to applications
pmc-13661827.creator: Faria Fatima, Syed Saqib Ali Zaidi, Yang Guang, He Huang, Xiao-Man Sun
pmc-13661827.description: Despite the widespread industrial applications of nanozymes, their usage is often limited by mechanistic factors. They lack reaction control with catalyst fouling, which limits catalytic turnover and makes nanozyme recovery an energy-intensive process at large scale. These mechanistic challenges have been addressed by the evolution of photoresponsiveness into nanozymes called as photonanozymes (PNZs).

uslaw-usc-t15-s1527a.title: 15 U.S.C. § 1527a — Economics and Statistics Administration Revolving Fund
uslaw-usc-t15-s1527a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s1527a.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 40 (Department Of Commerce). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. There is hereby established the Economics and Statistics Administration Revolving Fund which shall be available without fiscal year limitation. For initial capitalization, there is appropriated $1,677,000 to the Fund: Provided, That the Secretary of Commerce is authorized to disseminate economic and statistical data products.
